title: Segment users with TrustSec SGTs
domain: Secure Network Access, Visibility, and Enforcement
blurb: Tag users with security group tags in ISE, write a policy matrix, and enforce it on the switch.
purpose: VLANs and IP addresses make poor security boundaries as networks grow. This lab uses TrustSec to give users a Security Group Tag and enforce policy by group rather than by address. It covers software-defined segmentation.
scenario: Contractors and employees share VLAN 10, but only employees may reach the finance servers. Instead of IP-based ACLs, use **Cisco TrustSec**: ISE assigns a **security group tag (SGT)** at login, and the switch enforces a **policy matrix** between tags.
topology:
Employee (SGT 4) ─┐
                   ├─ SW1 ── Finance servers (SGT 10)
Contractor (SGT 5) ┘     ISE: policy matrix
objectives: Fill in the SGACL policy matrix in ISE
Turn on role-based enforcement on the switch

steps.title: The three TrustSec functions
steps.learn: TrustSec works in three stages. **Classification** assigns the tag, usually as an ISE authorization result. **Propagation** carries it, inline in the Ethernet frame (CMD header) or over **SXP** to devices that can't tag inline. **Enforcement** applies **SGACLs** based on the source and destination tags.
steps.task: Match each action to its TrustSec function.

fields.label: ISE returns SGT Employees in the Access-Accept
SXP sends IP-to-SGT mappings to a firewall
The switch drops contractor traffic to finance

steps.title: Fill in the policy matrix
steps.learn: In ISE, the **TrustSec policy matrix** has source tags as rows and destination tags as columns. Each cell holds an SGACL, such as **Permit IP** or **Deny IP**.
steps.task: Set **Employees → Finance_Servers** to **Permit IP** and **Contractors → Finance_Servers** to **Deny IP**. Leave the default at **Permit IP**.
steps.screen: ISE › Work Centers › TrustSec › TrustSec Policy › Matrix

steps.title: Turn on enforcement
steps.learn: The switch downloads the matrix cells it needs from ISE. `cts role-based enforcement` turns on SGACL enforcement for routed traffic, and the `vlan-list` form adds switched traffic within VLANs.
steps.task: Turn on role-based enforcement globally and for **VLAN 10**.
steps.hint: `cts role-based enforcement` and `cts role-based enforcement vlan-list 10`.

commands.explain: Turns on SGT-based enforcement on the switch.

commands.note: Traffic between tags in VLAN 10 is now checked against the matrix.
commands.explain: Enforces SGT policy on VLAN 10, where traffic is switched rather than routed.

steps.title: Why tags beat IP ACLs
steps.question: What's the main advantage of SGACLs over IP-based ACLs here?

options.text: The policy follows the user's role, not the IP address, so it keeps working when addresses change, and one matrix replaces ACLs on many devices.
SGACLs encrypt the traffic between groups.
options.why: TrustSec can be combined with MACsec, but SGACLs only permit or deny.
ISE classifies users and holds the matrix in this design.

steps.title: Verify the permissions
steps.task: Show the role-based permissions the switch downloaded.

commands.output:
IPv4 Role-based permissions default:
        Permit IP-00
IPv4 Role-based permissions from group 4:Employees to group 10:Finance_Servers:
        Permit IP-00
IPv4 Role-based permissions from group 5:Contractors to group 10:Finance_Servers:
        Deny IP-00
RBACL Monitor All for Dynamic Policies : FALSE
RBACL Monitor All for Configured Policies : FALSE
commands.note: Contractors are denied to finance, and employees are permitted.
commands.explain: Shows the SGACL permissions the switch downloaded from ISE.

summary: TrustSec classification by ISE, a policy matrix permitting employees and denying contractors to the finance servers, and SGACL enforcement on the switch for VLAN 10.
